results.name: Barbell Curtsy Lunge
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell across your upper back. Grip the bar with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Step your right leg behind and across your left leg, lowering your hips until your left thigh is parallel to the floor, and your right knee nearly touches the floor in a curtsy position.

Push through your front heel to return to the starting position. Repeat on the other side by stepping your left leg behind and across your right leg. Continue alternating legs for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure your front knee tracks over your toes to prevent knee injuries and ensure proper form.
Lower your body slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Keep your chest up and back straight throughout the movement to maintain proper alignment.
results.description: Barbell Curtsy Lunge is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Adductors.

results.name: Barbell Feet Elevated Figure Four Glute Bridge
instructions: Lie on your back with your arms to the floor. Place one foot on a box and cross the opposite ankle over your working leg, forming a figure-four shape. Position the barbell evenly across your hips, holding it securely with both hands.
Push through your elevated heel to lift your hips upward until your torso forms a straight line from shoulders to knee.
At the peak of the movement, squeeze your glutes. Slowly lower your hips down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired repetitions, and then switch legs and repeat.
tips: Ensure the barbell is comfortably cushioned or padded to prevent pressure on your hips.
Engage your core to prevent arching your back or overextending.
Exhale as you thrust up, and inhale as you return to the starting position.
results.description: Barbell Feet Elevated Figure Four Glute Bridge is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Lower Back, Core.

results.name: Barbell Feet Elevated Glute Bridge
instructions: Lie on your back with your feet placed on an elevated surface, knees bent. Rest a barbell across your hips, gripping it securely with both hands for stability.
Push through your elevated heels to lift your hips upward until your torso forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
At the peak of the movement, squeeze your glutes. Slowly lower your hips down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you lift your hips and inhale as you lower them.
Ensure your knees remain aligned with your feet; don’t let them collapse inward or flare outward.
Avoid excessive momentum; focus on a controlled, glute-driven motion.
results.description: Barbell Feet Elevated Glute Bridge is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Lower Back, Core.

results.name: Barbell Feet Elevated Single Leg Glute Bridge
instructions: Lie on your back with your arms to the floor. Place one foot on a box while the opposite leg is extended straight up. Position the barbell evenly across your hips, holding it securely with both hands.
Push through your elevated heel to lift your hips upward until your torso forms a straight line from shoulders to knee.
At the peak of the movement, squeeze your glutes. Slowly lower your hips down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired repetitions, and then switch legs and repeat.
tips: Drive through the heel of the elevated foot to emphasize glute activation.
Avoid arching your back; keep your core engaged throughout.
Exhale as you lift your hips; inhale as you lower them.
results.description: Barbell Feet Elevated Single Leg Glute Bridge is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Lower Back, Core.

results.name: Barbell Feet Elevated Staggered Glute Bridge
instructions: Lie on your back with your feet elevated on a box. Place one foot slightly forward and the other slightly backward (staggered stance). Rest a barbell across your hips, gripping it securely with both hands for stability.
Push through your elevated heels to lift your hips upward until your torso forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
At the peak of the movement, squeeze your glutes. Slowly lower your hips down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired repetitions, and then switch legs and repeat.
tips: Keep your head, neck, and shoulders relaxed throughout the movement.
Keep your core tight throughout the movement to stabilize your pelvis.
Ensure the barbell is positioned comfortably across your hips, using a pad if needed.
results.description: Barbell Feet Elevated Staggered Glute Bridge is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Lower Back, Core.

results.name: Barbell Front Bench Squat
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, back facing a bench, holding a barbell across your upper chest. Grip the bar with your hands shoulder-width apart, and keep your elbows pointing forward.
Begin the squat by pushing your hips back and bending your knees, lowering your body until you sit down on the bench.
Push through your heels to stand back up to the starting position, extending your hips and knees fully. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your elbows high to maintain the barbell's position on your chest.
Engage your core to support your lower back and maintain proper posture.
Lower your body slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
results.description: Barbell Front Bench Squat is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Lower Back.

results.name: Barbell Front Squat (Clean Grip)
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell across your upper chest. Grip the bar with your hands shoulder-width apart, and keep your elbows pointing forward.
Begin the squat by pushing your hips back and bending your knees, lowering your body until your thighs are parallel to the floor or slightly below.
Push through your heels to return to the starting position, extending your hips and knees fully. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Lower your body slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you push up and inhaling as you lower down.
Keep your chest up and back straight throughout the movement to maintain proper alignment.
results.description: Barbell Front Squat (Clean Grip) is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Lower Back.

results.name: Barbell Front Rack Lunge
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell across your upper chest. Grip the bar with your hands shoulder-width apart, and keep your elbows pointing forward.
Step forward with your right leg, lowering your body until your right thigh is parallel to the floor and your left knee nearly touches the floor.
Push through your front heel to return to the starting position. Repeat the movement with the same leg.
tips: Keep your elbows high to maintain the barbell's position on your chest.
Engage your core to support your lower back and maintain proper posture.
Lower your body slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
results.description: Barbell Front Rack Lunge is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves.

results.name: Barbell Front Squat
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and position a barbell on the front of your shoulders. Cross your arms over the barbell, with your elbows pointing forward and your upper arms parallel to the floor, holding the barbell tightly.
Lower your body into a squat position by bending your knees and pushing your hips back, keeping your weight on your heels.
Continue lowering until your thighs are parallel to the floor and then push through your heels to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you stand up from the squat and inhale as you lower into the squat.
Keep your chest up and avoid leaning forward excessively.
Focus on engaging your quadriceps and glutes throughout the movement.
results.description: Barbell Front Squat is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves, Core.

results.name: Barbell Full Squat (Side View)
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell across your upper back. Grip the bar with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Begin the squat by pushing your hips back and bending your knees, lowering your body until your thighs are slightly below than parallel to the floor.
Push through your heels to return to the starting position, extending your hips and knees fully. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your chest up and back straight to maintain proper posture and alignment.
Focus on driving through your heels to engage your glutes and quadriceps effectively.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you stand up and inhaling as you lower down.
results.description: Barbell Full Squat (Side View) is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Lower Back.
